fields.name: OxyPixel
fields.summary: Pixel-art drawing and animation with layers, Aseprite imports and sprite-atlas packing.
fields.description: A pixel-art editor with layered drawing, frame animation, tags, palettes and sprite-sheet export. Imports supported ASE/ASEPRITE documents for editing in its own OXYPix format. Its OxyPack atlas packer reads Aseprite files and emits game-engine PNG/JSON atlases; CLI and MCP tools share the editing core.
fields.limitations: Early release; full Aseprite behavior and plugin compatibility are not claimed. ASE imports convert to OXYPix rather than saving back: tilemaps become plain layers, reference layers are omitted and cel opacity is baked into pixels. Editing is limited to 1024 pixels per side, 256 frames and 32 layers. Windows downloads are unsigned.

screenshots.alt: OxyPixel: layered pixel-art scene and drawing tools.

fields.name: PixelCraft
fields.summary: Aseprite-style pixel art and animation with ASE file exchange, tilemaps, palettes and independent Lua extensions.
fields.description: A standalone pixel-art editor with layered drawing, frame animation, tilemaps, palettes and native project storage. Imports and exports supported ASE/ASEPRITE documents using the published format specification. Includes an embedded Lua runtime and an independent extension interface.
fields.limitations: Early alpha. Published v0.1.0 assets cover Linux; Windows installer workflows are documented but a released installer was not verified. Full ICC preview, arbitrary Aseprite Lua APIs, original themes and some ASE encodings or tileset arrangements are unsupported. Other platforms remain unvalidated.

notes: Only Linux AppImage release assets verified; Windows packaging workflow is not treated as a distributed/tested Windows app.

fields.name: Rook
fields.summary: Run Roblox place files in an independent Rust engine with Luau scripting, physics and client/server play.
fields.description: An independent implementation of the Roblox engine that reads and writes place/model files, runs Luau scripts and reproduces selected Instance APIs and services. Combines its own DataModel, scheduling and replication with open-source Luau, rbx-dom, Rapier and wgpu. Includes rendering, audio, terrain and inspection tools.
fields.limitations: Early development; file-loading and script-test results are maintainer-reported, not full game compatibility. GUI support remains in progress. Does not connect to Roblox servers or provide wire compatibility with the official client/server. Game places and assets must be supplied separately; some content resolution uses Roblox services.

fields.name: Sue
fields.summary: Clip Studio Paint-style illustration, comics and animation tools in a shared creative workspace.
fields.description: A creative workspace whose Sue Paint studio provides illustration, comics and animation workflows: pressure-sensitive brushes, stabilization, layers, blend modes, clipping, selections and canvas navigation. Shared project storage, undo, image viewing and conversion also serve its writing studio.
fields.limitations: Early software; native Clip Studio project, brush, material and service compatibility is not established. Uses its own SUE project container. Larger planned studios and AI runtimes are not implemented. The Sayn License requires the exact text Sayn was here in at least one file of distributions, modifications or incorporating projects. iOS packages require sideloading.

notes: Sayn LICENSE is MIT-like with an added exact-string attribution condition; recorded LicenseRef-Sayn, not MIT.
Hosted build is the user-supplied /try/ URL. Native CSP format/material/service compatibility not inferred from painting UI.

fields.name: OxyBrush
fields.summary: ZBrush-style digital sculpting with brushes, subdivision levels, voxel remeshing and OBJ/STL exchange.
fields.description: A digital-clay sculpting application with pressure-sensitive brushes, masking, symmetry, multi-piece scenes, subdivision levels, voxel remeshing, decimation and face groups. Saves its own OXB projects with autosave/recovery and imports or exports OBJ and STL geometry.
fields.limitations: Alpha; native ZBrush file interoperability is research, not shipped support. Dynamic topology, vertex color, sculpt layers, posing, UVs and baking remain planned. Tablet pressure and high-poly performance need qualification. Windows builds are unsigned and macOS packages are not notarized; iPad is planned.

screenshots.alt: OxyBrush: sculpting viewport, brush controls and model pieces.

fields.name: HumanMotionCraft
fields.summary: Cascadeur-style humanoid animation with IK, keyframes, physics-assisted posing and learned in-betweening.
fields.description: A broader alternative for Cascadeur-style 3D humanoid animation. Provides a built-in humanoid rig, keyframes, layers, IK pins, physics-assisted posing, motion-matching locomotion and learned in-betweening. Desktop, CLI and MCP commands share the same core and export GLB animation clips.
fields.limitations: Not a Spine 2D replacement or a full Cascadeur clone; native Cascadeur project compatibility is not established. Focuses on humanoids rather than arbitrary rigs, character creation or a full 3D scene editor. Published releases are Windows-only; Linux builds are documented. Optional motion-from-text helpers require separate models with their own licenses.

fields.name: ModelCraft
fields.summary: eDrawings-style CAD viewing with SolidWorks and Revit readers, measurements, sections and assembly inspection.
fields.description: An independent CAD viewer for eDrawings-style inspection of SolidWorks parts/assemblies, Revit documents and common interchange formats. Provides an assembly tree, measurements, section planes, visibility controls and image capture. Format readers use independent code and documented open-source libraries; it is separate from getcadcraft ModelCraft.
fields.limitations: MIT is declared in the README, NOTICE and Cargo metadata; a standalone project license text was not found. Some interface code is adapted from PdfCraft; bundled components retain their own licenses. Format coverage is partial and maintainer-reported. Some formats need optional Open CASCADE, assimp or web-ifc builds. This is a viewer, not a CAD authoring replacement.

fields.name: encoderCraft
fields.summary: An early Media Encoder-style queue, preset and watch-folder prototype with codec and automation components.
fields.description: An early Adobe Media Encoder-style prototype with queue management, presets, watch folders, a desktop interface and CLI/MCP automation. Includes codec and media-pipeline components built on craft-libs. Source-media transcoding is not connected to the current export pipeline.
fields.limitations: Not a usable general-purpose Media Encoder replacement. The current export pipeline generates blank video frames and silent audio rather than decoding the selected input. Native AME project and Adobe integration compatibility are unverified. README/Cargo declare MIT OR Apache-2.0, but the referenced project license files are absent.

fields.name: Drop
fields.summary: Self-host a Steam-style library to browse, distribute, install and launch your own DRM-free games.
fields.description: A self-hosted game-distribution platform with a library storefront, metadata imports, user accounts and a desktop client for downloading, installing and launching operator-supplied DRM-free games. Reimplements a subset of Steam-style library and distribution workflows on infrastructure the operator controls.
fields.limitations: A broader alternative, not a compatible Steam client or replacement for Valve accounts, DRM, purchases, Workshop or multiplayer services. Requires a self-hosted server and separately supplied games. Upstream is in maintenance mode with bug fixes and external contributions still accepted; client packages vary by platform.

fields.name: GameDepot
fields.summary: Self-host a Steam-style game depot with library management, chunked delivery and a native desktop client.
fields.description: A self-hosted Steam-style game distribution and preservation platform, developed as a hard fork of Drop OSS. Retains library, account and desktop-client workflows while developing storefront ingestion, content-addressed chunk delivery, deduplication and mesh-networking integrations. Uses TypeScript/Svelte services and Rust transfer components.
fields.limitations: Early fork; release maturity and broad roadmap completion are not independently verified. Does not reproduce Steam accounts, DRM, store purchases, Workshop or service APIs. Store adapters and networking depend on external projects and services; inherited components retain their respective licenses.

fields.name: GameVault
fields.summary: A source-available, self-hosted Steam-style library for DRM-free games, downloads and playtime tracking.
fields.description: A source-available Steam-style platform for hosting an operator-supplied DRM-free game library. The server indexes games and metadata, manages accounts and distributes files to separate desktop and web clients, which provide installation, launching, library browsing and playtime/progress tracking.
fields.limitations: Source-available under a noncommercial license, not open-source software. Does not replace Steam purchases, accounts, DRM or service APIs. Requires a server and separately supplied games; client implementations live in separate repositories. GameVault 2 clients are public beta, with GameVault+ features still missing.

notes: Maintainer requested this GameVault after the domain ambiguity was explained.
CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 is source-available/noncommercial, not an open-source license; disclosed in description, limitations and comment.
Backend is primary repository; native/web clients are separate implementations in the same Phalcode product ecosystem.
